q1_issues.issue: (Inheritance cattle perfect) asserts that cattle are perfect simpliciter, whereas the sentence predicates perfection only relative to the food-factory role ('perfect AS food factories'), so splitting the adjective off the predicate nominal over-asserts.
The predication is metaphorical, and taken literally (with the genus atom) it derives that cattle are a subtype of factory, which the sentence does not claim.

q2_gaps: metaphorical predicate nominal ('cattle are food factories') — the instruction set has an idiom coherence test but no treatment of metaphor, so the literal Inheritance plus its mandatory genus asserts cattle ⊑ factory

evaluative / role-relative adjective inside a predicate NOMINAL ('perfect food factories') — the adjective+noun split rule is stated for referring NPs ('a dented pail') and the comparison-class escape hatch (Degree X scale (forKind N)) only fires on explicit 'ADJ for a N' wording, so nothing says how to scope an adjective that modifies the predicated role rather than the entity
notes: The mechanics are right: bare-plural generic → Inheritance at 0.9/0.9, food_factory fused as a classifying modifier_noun with its genus emitted and the noun modifier 'food' correctly not exposed. Both q1 issues trace to the coverage gaps rather than to a misapplied rule.
